name: Account Takeover via Password Reset Poisoning
description: Manipulate Host header during password reset to redirect the reset link to attacker-controlled domain. User clicks link in email, token sent to attacker.
steps: Intercept POST /forgot-password
Modify Host header to attacker.com
User receives email with link to attacker.com/reset?token=XXX
Attacker captures token, resets password
detection: Host header manipulation in password reset flow
No validation of Host header against allowed origins

name: OAuth Token Theft via Open Redirect
description: Chain open redirect with OAuth flow to steal access tokens. redirect_uri validation bypassed via subdomain or path traversal.
steps: Find open redirect on target domain
Craft OAuth URL with redirect_uri=target.com/redirect?url=attacker.com
Victim authorizes, token sent to attacker via fragment or query
detection: Loose redirect_uri validation in OAuth config

name: Race Condition in Payment/Transfer
description: Exploit TOCTOU race condition in financial transactions. Send concurrent requests to withdraw/transfer more than available balance.
steps: Identify balance-deducting endpoint
Send 50+ concurrent requests with same amount
Backend checks balance before atomic deduction
Multiple requests pass check before first deduction commits
detection: No database-level locking on financial operations

name: GraphQL Introspection + IDOR Combo
description: Use GraphQL introspection to discover hidden types and fields, then exploit missing authorization on object access.
steps: Query __schema to enumerate all types
Find User/Admin types with sensitive fields
Query other users' data without authorization check
Access admin-only mutations via discovered schema

name: SSRF to Cloud Metadata to RCE
description: Chain SSRF to access cloud metadata service, extract IAM credentials, then use those creds to execute commands or access S3 buckets.
steps: Find SSRF via URL parameter or webhook
Access http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/
Extract AccessKeyId, SecretAccessKey, Token
Use AWS CLI with stolen creds to access internal resources
detection: Any user-controlled URL fetch without SSRF protection
Application running on AWS/GCP/Azure with instance roles

name: Prototype Pollution to XSS/RCE
description: Pollute Object.prototype via merge/extend operations, then trigger XSS via DOM clobbering or RCE via server-side gadgets.
steps: Find endpoint that deep-merges user input
Send __proto__[polluted]=true
Find gadget: template engine reads from prototype
Achieve XSS or RCE depending on gadget
detection: Deep merge of user input without prototype filtering

name: JWT Algorithm Confusion Attack
description: Switch JWT algorithm from RS256 to HS256. Server uses public key as HMAC secret, attacker signs arbitrary tokens.
steps: Obtain public key (/.well-known/jwks.json or certificate)
Create JWT with alg:HS256, set claims to admin
Sign with the public key as HMAC secret
Server verifies HS256 signature using public key = valid
detection: No strict algorithm enforcement on verification

name: Stored XSS via File Upload (SVG/HTML)
description: Upload SVG or HTML file containing JavaScript. When other users view the file, XSS executes in their browser context.
steps: Create SVG with embedded <script> tag
Upload as profile picture or document
File served from same origin without Content-Disposition: attachment
Victim views file, XSS triggers

name: Mass Assignment Privilege Escalation
description: Include admin/role fields in profile update request. Server blindly applies all fields from request body to database model.
steps: Update profile with normal fields
Add role=admin or isAdmin=true to request body
Server applies all fields without whitelist
Attacker gains admin privileges
detection: No field whitelist on update operations

name: SSTI to RCE via Template Engine
description: Inject template syntax into user-controllable field that gets rendered server-side. Escalate from expression evaluation to command execution.
steps: Find input reflected in rendered page
Test {{7*7}} — if 49 appears, SSTI confirmed
Identify template engine (Jinja2, Twig, EJS, etc)
Use engine-specific gadget chain to achieve RCE
detection: User input passed to template render function

name: HTTP Request Smuggling (CL.TE)
description: Exploit Content-Length vs Transfer-Encoding parsing differences between front-end and back-end servers to smuggle requests.
steps: Send request with both CL and TE headers
Front-end uses CL, back-end uses TE (or vice versa)
Smuggled request processed as next user's request prefix
Capture other users' requests or bypass access controls
detection: Multiple proxy layers with different HTTP parsers
Both CL and TE headers accepted simultaneously

name: NoSQL Injection Authentication Bypass
description: Use MongoDB query operators in login request to bypass authentication. $ne, $gt operators always evaluate to true.
steps: Send login with {"email":{"$ne":""},"password":{"$ne":""}}
MongoDB query matches first user where email != '' AND password != ''
Returns first admin account typically
Full authentication bypass
detection: MongoDB/Mongoose queries built from user input
No schema validation on login parameters
Object type not enforced (allows operator injection)

name: Path Traversal to Source Code Disclosure
description: Exploit path traversal in file download/view endpoints to read application source code, config files, or /etc/passwd.
steps: Find file download endpoint with filename parameter
Try ../../../etc/passwd
If filtered, try double encoding: ..%252f..%252f
Read source code for further vulnerabilities
detection: User input in file path operations
No path canonicalization before file access

name: Subdomain Takeover
description: Claim abandoned cloud resources (S3, Heroku, GitHub Pages) pointed to by target's DNS CNAME records.
steps: Enumerate subdomains via DNS bruteforce
Find CNAME pointing to unclaimed resource (e.g., app-xyz.herokuapp.com)
Register the resource name on the platform
Serve malicious content on target's subdomain
detection: Dangling DNS records pointing to external services
NoSuchBucket or similar errors on subdomains

name: WebSocket Cross-Site Hijacking
description: WebSocket endpoints that don't verify Origin header allow cross-site connections. Attacker's page can read victim's WebSocket data.
steps: Find WebSocket endpoint without Origin validation
Create malicious page that connects to ws://target.com/ws
Victim visits attacker's page while authenticated
Attacker reads all WebSocket messages meant for victim
detection: No Origin header check on WebSocket upgrade
Authentication only via cookies (no CSRF token)
